To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) argumentative writing support can be automated, (b) humans agree on identifying argumentation structures and assessing the quality of arguments, (c) the automatic identification of arguments is feasible and (d) the quality of arguments can be assessed automatically.

humans are able to reliably apply an annotation scheme that identifies argumentation structures in essays, that a novel joint model for argument parsing considerably improves the performance over state-of-the-art approaches and that myside biases and insufficiently supported arguments can be recognized with high accuracy.

(i) humans can reliably identify argumentation structures in natural language texts and (ii) computational models can be trained to identify argumentation structures and to assess arguments with substantial performance.

the analysis of argumentative writing and contributes to a deeper understanding of argumentative writing support and computational argumentation.

the results of this thesis provide a foundation for the design of argumentative writing support tools that can provide feedback about the structure and quality of written arguments.
this thesis provides the first step towards automated argumentative writing support by means of natural language processing.
the research results of this thesis have a significant contribution to the field of argumentative writing support and computational argumentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a novel corpus annotated with finegrained argumentation structures.
we introduce a novel annotation scheme that is capable of identifying consistent argumentation struc- tures in persuasive essays.
we have introduced a novel corpus annotated with argumentation structures and we have proposed novel approaches for assessing the merits and defects for written arguments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
argumentative writing support can benefit from recent advances in natural language processing and computational argumentation.
computational argumentation can provide novel writing support systems that help students to improve their writing skills and to become more aware of the merits and defects in their own arguments.
argumentative writing support is feasible using natural language processing methods.
